svg.title: Four quantitative bounds on useful agent scale
svg.desc: Four panels. Top left: effective independent opinions against nominal calls on a logarithmic axis; curves for correlation 0.01, 0.1 and 0.5 flatten at ceilings of 100, 10 and 2 — a million calls buy one over rho analysts. Top right: Amdahl speedup against team size; a serial fraction of 5 per cent caps speedup at 20 times, 30 per cent at about 3 times. Bottom left: chain success probability against chain length; per-step reliability 0.99 falls to 37 per cent by 100 steps while 0.999 holds 90 per cent. Bottom right: sampled checks needed to certify an error bound stay flat as corpus size grows from ten thousand to a million — 300 checks for 1 per cent, 3,000 for 0.1 per cent.
svg.text: Four bounds on useful scale — each one a ceiling that more agents cannot lift
Redundancy: a million calls buy 1/ρ analysts
agents (log) — sixteen or a million, same ceiling
Sampled assurance: ≈3/p checks, flat in N
corpus size N — the census-class economics
